utility.notes: Concord's own Community Choice Energy (MCE) page confirms: 'the existing electrical utility, PG&E, delivers that power, continuing the metering and billing for customers.' PG&E is the underlying transmission/distribution/billing utility; MCE is a separate default generation supplier — see generation_supplier.

value.name: MCE (Marin Clean Energy) - Light Green (default service)
value.notes: Concord's own page states MCE 'began providing the City of Concord with an alternative to PG&E' in 2018, and that customers who take no action are 'automatically enrolled in MCE's "Light Green" power supply, which is made up of 50% renewable power' as the default, with 'Deep Green' (100% renewable) and 'Local Sol' (100% local solar) available as opt-up choices.

county.notes: Concord's own MCE page identifies MCE as 'Contra Costa County's community-based electricity provider' in the context of Concord's own enrollment, structurally confirming the city-county relationship; no single page was found this session stating the relationship as one direct standalone sentence.

permit_authority.value: City of Concord Building Division (Community and Economic Development Department)

interconnection_url.notes: Same PG&E-wide Net Energy Metering program URL already verified for the Fremont/Oakland/Berkeley/Richmond records — reused as a utility-level fact. pge.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch; confirmed to exist via search engine indexing under its expected title.

value.name: California SGIP - current category and budget check required
value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

battery_programs.notes: SGIP program data refreshed on 2026-08-26 from the official 2026 Handbook and live Program Metrics. Earlier locality records contained 2025 opening/availability language. This record does not assert household eligibility, reservation availability, or a guaranteed incentive; current category and program-administrator status must be checked before reliance.

value.name: Contractor's Declaration (licensed contractors) or Owner-Builder Acknowledgement and Information Verification Form
SolarAPP+ approved checklist (if submitting under the 'Solar PV (Solar APP)' permit type with a SolarAPP+ approval ID — no other design documents required in that case)
Drawings (Cover Sheet, Roof Plan, Single Line Electrical Diagram, Signage/Labeling) — Standard Plans PV-1 through PV-4 may be used
Manufacturer Data Sheets (PV modules, mounting systems, combiner boxes, inverters, disconnects)
Mounting bracket attachment details (fastener size/spacing/location, existing roof structure and material)
Structural Information Worksheet (WKS-1) and, if system exceeds 5 lbs/sq ft, Structural Calculations by a licensed engineer
Electrical Information Worksheet (WKS-2) and Equipment Schedule
Business License (all contractors doing work within the City)

required_documents.notes: Combines the City's own Residential Solar PV Submittal Requirements checklist (SR-RSOLAR, effective 9/15/2023) and Standardized Permit Submittal Instructions (Information Bulletin IB-010, effective 8/5/2020). The standard (non-SolarAPP+) submittal path requires the full document set; the SolarAPP+ path only requires the approved SolarAPP+ checklist.

value: Inspection appointments can be scheduled for the following day
Every effort is made to limit the inspection window waiting period to four hours or less, depending on daily volume and staff availability
Required inspections may include electrical and final; the inspector verifies conformance with code requirements and the approved plans
After the final building inspection, contact PG&E — the PV system is not approved to energize until PG&E has inspected the system and installed the net meter

value.notes: The City's own Information Bulletin IB-010 states: 'every attempt will be made to complete the permit review process expeditiously or within three full business days after filing of a complete permit application packet depending on staff availability and workload constraints,' for standard installations (10kW or less, single-family residential rooftop, meeting all prescriptive requirements).

value.program_or_pathway: Streamlined permit process (Information Bulletin IB-010) for standard installations, or SolarAPP+
other_conditions: Up to 10kW on single-family residential rooftops (1 & 2 unit dwellings/Group R-3, including duplexes); does not include new structures like trellises, patio covers, or canopies
Existing roof must have one layer of roofing, array weight 5 lbs/sq ft or less, concentrated load under 50 lbs per attachment for the streamlined path
Systems with battery back-up are not eligible for the standard/streamlined installation path and must go through normal permit review with a registered electrical engineer design
No planning/zoning review required for rooftop solar consistent with this bulletin; rooftop solar is statutorily CEQA-exempt under SB 226

permit_fees.notes: The City's own Information Bulletin IB-010 states 'Residential rooftop solar permit fees are computed on actual costs associated with the City's permit review and inspection process' per the Master Fee Schedule, but gives no specific dollar figure or formula.
